steps.description: Enter the domain part of your email address, meaning everything after the @. For example, if your address is pastor@gracechurch.org, the domain is gracechurch.org. The server settings below will be reused by any Email Account that points at this domain.
steps.label: Domain Name
steps.title: Domain Name

steps.description: Hostname of your incoming mail server, meaning the server you fetch messages from. Examples: imap.gmail.com, outlook.office365.com, mail.gracechurch.org. Your email provider's help docs list this; search “IMAP settings”.
steps.label: Incoming Server
steps.title: Incoming Server

steps.description: Leave this checked for IMAP (recommended) so that read/unread state and folders stay in sync between Frappe and your other mail clients. Uncheck only if your provider supports just POP3.
steps.label: Use IMAP
steps.title: Use IMAP

steps.description: Encrypt the incoming connection. Leave checked in almost all cases, since modern providers require it.
steps.label: Use SSL
steps.title: Use SSL

steps.description: Port for the incoming server. Common values: 993 for IMAP+SSL, 995 for POP3+SSL, 143 for plain IMAP. If unsure, try 993.
steps.label: Incoming Port
steps.title: Incoming Port

steps.description: Hostname of your outgoing mail server, meaning where Frappe sends messages from. Examples: smtp.gmail.com, smtp.office365.com, mail.gracechurch.org. Search your provider's docs for “SMTP settings”.
steps.label: Outgoing Server
steps.title: Outgoing Server

steps.description: Encrypt the outgoing connection with STARTTLS (modern default). Leave checked unless your provider explicitly says otherwise.
steps.label: Use TLS
steps.title: Use TLS

steps.description: Port for the outgoing server. Common values: 587 with TLS (most common), 465 with SSL, 25 plain (rarely allowed). If unsure, try 587.
steps.label: Outgoing Port
steps.title: Outgoing Port
